name: What is the best order for planning a whole-home remodel?

mainEntity.name: What is the best order for planning a whole-home remodel?
mainEntity.text: What is the best order for planning a whole-home remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: A smart remodel starts with priorities, not finishes. First decide what problems the project must solve, what rooms matter most, and how much disruption you can tolerate. Next set a realistic budget, including contingency, so design decisions stay grounded. After that, define the scope in enough detail that the contractor and design team know exactly what is being built. Once the scope is set, move into drawings, engineering if needed, and permits. Contractor selection should happen with plans and scope in hand so bids can be compared fairly. Construction should begin only after approvals, selections, and logistics are largely settled. This sequence reduces the chance of costly redesigns and schedule drift. Many homeowners reverse the order by choosing finishes first or asking for pricing before the scope is clear, which makes comparisons unreliable. In Los Angeles remodeling, especially for high-end homes, the best results come from sequencing decisions carefully before demolition starts. That planning discipline also improves coordination between designers, builders, and inspectors.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best order is goals, budget, scope, design, permits, contractor selection, and then construction. Skipping steps or choosing finishes before the scope is defined usually leads to change orders and delays.
